messages:

Subject: Re: Demo and benchmark discussion

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — that was helpful. A few items from our side: we need to understand how an open-model route would compare to our current in-house model (Ledgerly-prop-v1) for our invoice-parsing product. Key concerns are: precision on extracted fields, occasional hallucinations on ambiguous lines, and token-level latency for 8k context prompts.

Immediate asks:
- Can you send a concise recommendation (2–3 models) to trial, and what each would cost per 1M tokens?
- Share any example prompts and a minimal prompt bundle we can run locally during the POC.
- Acceptance thresholds we should validate against (precision / hallucination / latency).

I'll loop in Samir on implementation scheduling — we can reproduce a small eval set from our sandbox.

Thanks,
Dana Lopez
Head of ML, Ledgerly

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Demo and benchmark discussion

Dana — great questions. Short version up top, details below.

Recommendation (trial shortlist):
1) Llama-3-34B (q4f32) — strong instruction-following, good extraction fidelity on structured text; best balance for quality/latency.
2) RedPajama-Chat-13B-instruct — lower cost, competitive on precision with prompt engineering; faster inference on some instance types.
3) Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) — lowest cost, good for high-throughput but may need additional post-processing to hit precision thresholds.

Proprietary baseline: Ledgerly-prop-v1 — from our discussion it sounds like parity targets should measure against your current metrics.

Suggested acceptance thresholds (first-pass):
- Field-level extraction F1 >= 0.92 for required fields (invoice_number, total_amount, due_date)
- Hallucination incidence < 3% on evaluation records (explicitly: spurious fields not present in input)
- 95th-percentile token latency < 180ms for 8k-context inference on your preferred instance class

Cost estimates (ballpark per 1M tokens, hosted):
- Llama-3-34B (q4f32): ~$1,200
- RedPajama-Chat-13B: ~$480
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8): ~$220

Next steps we propose:
1) You share an anonymized eval set (200–500 records) + 1–2 production prompts.
2) We spin a 2-week trial with the 3 candidate models; we deliver a comparison CSV and a short regen report.
3) Checkpoint after week 1 to adjust prompt bundle and acceptance thresholds.

I attached a starter prompt bundle and a small benchmark template you can run locally. We'll also push a reproducible eval notebook to the Drive link below.

Happy to set a 30-min sync tomorrow to align on the eval set and schedule.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a bit more color on evaluation methodology and deliverables.

What we'll deliver for the 2-week trial:
- Evaluation CSV (see attached: ledgerly_benchmark_results.csv) with per-record metrics (precision/recall/F1), hallucination flags, example model outputs and latency samples.
- Prompt bundle (the one Priyom shared) plus a set of 6 adversarial prompts that tend to trigger hallucination in bookkeeping data.
- Short regression checklist: prompt set versioning, acceptance thresholds spreadsheet (attached: acceptance_thresholds.xlsx), and a plan for automatic comparison back to your baseline.

Benchmarks & reproducibility:
- Notebook: https://docs.redwood.com/evals/ledgerly-postdemo (will be runnable with your anonymized eval set).
- HubSpot record: HS-Contact-87432 (for tracking the POC and ops steps).

A couple of practical notes:
- If the open models hit precision parity but show a higher hallucination variance, we'll propose a mitigation sprint (prompt templates + small post-filtering heuristics) before recommending a rollout.
- If latency is a blocker at your target instance class, we can test quantized variants and a short caching strategy for repeated templates.

Propose we lock the eval set by Friday (18 Jun) and begin the trial on Monday (21 Jun). If that works for you, Samir — could you confirm the anonymized dataset availability and whether you prefer hosted trial vs. private (VPC) evaluation?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
